questions.prompt: What is the capital city of India?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the India article.

questions.proof: The capital city of India is New Delhi.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with India?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture India on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the India article.

questions.proof: Its Andaman and Nicobar Islands share water borders with Indonesia, Myanmar and Thailand.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of India?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Name” part of the India article.

questions.proof: The preferred endonym (the name given to the country by its own people) is "Bhārat" in Hindi and other Indian languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It has six neighbours: _____ in the northwest; China, Nepal and Bhutan in the north; Bangladesh and Myanmar in the east; and Sri Lanka and the Maldives are nearby to the south.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “neighbours”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the India article.

questions.proof: It has six neighbours: Pakistan in the northwest; China, Nepal and Bhutan in the north; Bangladesh and Myanmar in the east; and Sri Lanka and the Maldives are nearby to the south.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “India has the fourth largest number of spoken languages per country in the world, only behind Papua New _____, Indonesia, and Nigeria.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Indonesia”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the India article.

questions.proof: India has the fourth largest number of spoken languages per country in the world, only behind Papua New Guinea, Indonesia, and Nigeria.
